summary: an optional `gateTimeoutMs` bounds every child the engine runs on a gate's behalf; the deadline reached kills the tree and the gate fails naming the deadline and the command
acceptance: a declared gate deadline bounds every child the engine spawns for a gate, a runner's operations included; a child that reaches it is killed under the declared grace and its gate fails the way a gate that threw does, naming the deadline and the command — and a chain declaring none gets no cap, as the per-invocation one already does
tests: a gate child that outlives the declared deadline is killed and its gate fails naming the deadline
a declared gate deadline is read per tick off the tick's own chain
pins: a chain declaring no gate deadline bounds no gate child
the harness package declares a gate deadline for its consumers

interface.changes: a chain may declare `supervisorPolicy.gateTimeoutMs`, read per tick beside the per-invocation cap, and the harness package declares one for consumers who adopt it
interface.hides: that only the agent invocation was bounded, so every gate, runner operation and restore the engine ran could wait forever with nothing reporting it
interface.rejected: a per-gate deadline and a `blamesSpan: false` on timeout — the engine cannot tell a span's runaway test from a gate's own stall, so attributing one would be inferred; a gate that stalls on every span is the abort backstop's to stop

notes: Operator ruling: one optional supervisor knob, no engine default (a default is mechanism only when a tick cannot run without one), and a timed-out gate rides the existing failure path with no new result field. The package's default is generous — a ceiling, not a budget; a merge here was measured at 16 minutes. `spec/chain.md`, *Supervisor policy is a chain-overridable default* enumerates the block and does not carry this field yet: the spec gap is named in this tick's body.
